responsibility: Implements the Xtensa backend’s executable target logic behind the declarations in xtensa.h/xtensa-protos.h and the patterns in xtensa.md. This file installs and defines most target hooks for option override and conditional register usage, register classes and mode validity, address legitimacy and TLS/PIC address handling, constant and section selection, cost modeling, calling convention and varargs/va_list handling, return-value placement, builtin folding/expansion, trampolines, frame layout and elimination decisions, and assorted assembly-output helpers. It also owns Xtensa-specific RTL expansion and late machine-dependent reorganization, including the hardware doloop rewrite pass that turns recognized loop_end RTL into Xtensa hardware loop sequences or falls back to explicit decrement-and-branch code, making it the central C implementation of Xtensa ABI, code-generation, and post-reload behavior.
same_name_distinction: Among the xtensa.* files, this is the executable backend implementation in C: it defines the Xtensa target hooks and helper routines that act on GCC IR/RTL, including option-driven behavior and the hardware doloop reorganization pass, whereas xtensa.h provides compile-time target macros/ABI definitions, xtensa.md supplies declarative RTL instruction patterns and scheduling data, and xtensa.opt declares the command-line options and target variables those implementations use.
